Animations.html.title: Animated SVGs | SVGImage
Animations.html.summary: Animated SVGs SVGImage plays supported SVG animations using native WPF animation clocks: <svg:SVGImage UriSource="animation.svg" UseAnimations="True" SizeType="ViewBoxToSizeNoStretch" /> UseAnimations defaults to true. It also works when the source is changed after initialization. Set it to false to render the static document. With SVGRender, opt in before loading: var renderer = new SVGImage.SVG.SVGRender { UseAnimations = true }; DrawingGroup drawing = renderer.LoadDrawing(filename); Supported timing includes numeric begin offsets, finite or indefinite repeatCount, fill="freeze", explicit keyTimes, linear/discrete interpolation and keySplines. Motion animation supports inline paths, local mpath references, path tangents (auto/auto-reverse), numeric rotation and keyPoints with keyTimes. Supported SMIL properties are animateTransform translation, scale, rotation and skew, timed display/visibility, opacity, circle/ellipse radii and center coordinates, and root viewBox camera movement. Additive transforms compose in SVG order. Animations can target their parent or a local href/xlink:href reference. CSS @keyframes supports transform and opacity animations, grouped offsets, multiple animations, shorthand and longhand declarations, positive/negative delays, fractional/indefinite iterations, reverse/alternate directions, fill modes and an initially paused state. Timing functions include the ease presets, cubic-bezier curves and the steps jump modes. Matching transform functions interpolate their parameters, preserving full rotations. Static/animated transforms support transform-origin with view-box or fill-box reference bounds. CSS must be included in a <style> element in the SVG; an HTML page's external styles are not automatically loaded. Styles may occur after their targets. Percentage translations, general transform-matrix decomposition and interactive play-state changes are not implemented. symbol/use rendering honors symbol viewBoxes, use viewport dimensions, alignment and aspect ratio. This is needed for Flash2Svg exports that assemble facial parts from symbols. Static matrix/saturation color filters used by these exports are applied to vector paint colors. Raster turbulence/displacement filter chains are described in Rendering.md; animated filter parameters are not implemented. For deterministic snapshots or exports, stop playback at an exact time: renderer.SeekAnimations(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(25)); // Render drawing into a RenderTargetBitmap, for example. SeekAnimations stops playback and evaluates the existing drawing; load/recreate the drawing to restart its native clocks. The same method is available on the control. For SMIL click-start timing, explicitly forward an event: svgControl.TriggerAnimationEvent("playButton", "click"); // Or renderer.TriggerAnimationEvent("playButton", "click"). This starts tracks whose begin names playButton.click, including numeric offsets. The control does not infer SVG element hit targets; the host decides which element/event to forward. Numeric event timing can also be used with snapshots. SVGRender.AnimationWarnings reports unsupported animated attributes and malformed SMIL tracks. Flash2Svg's empty final spline segment is treated as linear. JavaScript, HTML audio/foreignObject playback, path morphing, syncbase timing, animated masks and CSS layout/background animations are not implemented. In particular, the LoveDota example's visual camera/character timeline renders, while its JavaScript-triggered embedded audio is not played. The regression suite includes synthetic timing, sprite-sheet, live-clock, symbol viewport, camera and color-filter checks. Downloaded examples are deliberately kept outside this repository. To additionally validate local copies of the Flash2Svg examples and extracted CodePen horse, set SVG_ANIMATION_EXAMPLES to a folder containing Flash2Svg.wiki/img/*.svg and horse.svg, then run the regression runner. The extra checks load every file, trigger click-start timelines where present and require a changed rendered frame.

CSS.html.title: SVG author styles | SVGImage
CSS.html.summary: SVG author styles SVGImage supports type, universal, ID, class, compound, attribute-presence/equality and :root selectors, selector lists, and descendant, child and sibling combinators. The author cascade accounts for presentation attributes, selector specificity, source order, inline declarations and !important. Class attribute order does not alter precedence. Unsupported selector/conditional-rule blocks are ignored rather than applied globally. Custom properties inherit computed values and support var() substitutions, nested fallbacks and cycle detection. CSS-wide inherit/initial/unset keywords are resolved for the supported presentation-property subset. Styles also apply to gradient stops. currentColor inherits through shape groups. The declaration tokenizer preserves quoted strings, comments, function arguments and data URI separators. Styles are collected before shapes are constructed, so style elements may occur after their targets. See animation support for CSS timing, keyframes and transforms. This remains an SVG-focused subset: dynamic pseudo-classes, selector escapes/namespaces, advanced selectors, cascade layers, conditional media/supports rules, calc(), CSS layout and external HTML-page styles are not implemented.

Changelog.html.title: Changelog | SVGImage
Changelog.html.summary: Changelog Changes to SVGImage are recorded here, newest first. Dates use the project's local calendar (Europe/Berlin). Unreleased These entries describe the current repository source. They have not been assigned a NuGet release version. Install a published package for its released feature set, or build the current source to use these additions. 2026-10-29 Added Documentation: redesigned homepage and repository overview, original WPF-rendered gallery, support reference, getting-started guide and this permanent changelog. SVG filter graphs: standalone raster rendering, named in / in2 / result connections, SourceGraphic / SourceAlpha, filter regions, primitive subregions, coordinate units and sRGB / linearRGB processing. Procedural effects: four-channel seeded feTurbulence with turbulence/fractal noise, one/two base frequencies, octaves and stitching; feDisplacementMap with unpremultiplied channel selection and bilinear sampling. More filter primitives: feFlood, feOffset, feMerge, feComposite, feColorMatrix (matrix, saturation, hue rotation, luminance-to-alpha), feComponentTransfer (identity, table, discrete, linear, gamma), feBlend, feGaussianBlur, feMorphology and feTile. Text on a path: local textPath references, glyph placement and tangent rotation, percentage startOffset, text anchoring and styled spans. SMIL motion: animateMotion with inline paths or local mpath references, automatic/numeric rotation and keyPoints / keyTimes. Nested SVG viewports: independent percentage contexts, placement and sizing, viewBox mapping, meet/slice/none and overflow clipping. Symbol viewBoxes establish their content's percentage context too. Pattern painting: independent tile/content units, tile positions/dimensions, viewBoxes, transforms, opacity and forward href templates. Patterns are generated per target bounds. CSS cascade: specificity/source order, presentation/inline declarations, !important, CSS-wide keywords, inherited custom properties, nested var() fallbacks and cycle handling. CSS selectors: type, universal, ID, class, compound and attribute presence/equality selectors, :root, descendant/child and adjacent/general sibling relationships. CSS animation controls: multiple animations, shorthand/longhands, positive/negative delays, fractional repeats, directions, fill modes, initial paused state, grouped offsets and per-keyframe easing. Matching transform functions preserve full rotations. CSS colors: RGB/RGBA and HSL/HSLA functions, percentage channels, short/long RGBA hex colors, grey aliases and rebeccapurple. Regression coverage: an optional local resvg test-suite runner for 196 path/point/filter cases and eight turbulence references. Downloaded fixtures remain outside the repository. Fixed Middle/end text anchoring now shifts text before its anchor using advances; textPath respects its own anchor style. The native documentation gallery exposed this existing alignment issue. Clip paths unite child silhouettes and honor paths, basic shapes, text, use, inherited clip-rule, transforms, bounding-box units and forward references. Empty clips safely hide their targets. Recursive use references stop instead of overflowing the stack. Rendering restores the referenced shape's original parent. Paths preserve completed segments before invalid data, accept adjacent single-token arc flags and reflect curve controls. Point lists preserve valid pairs, ignore unmatched final coordinates and safely handle missing data. Element opacity is applied after filtering; fill/stroke opacity remains part of SourceGraphic. User-space generators can paint empty groups; tiling preserves input subregions and their transparent pixels. Radial focal points use the center's coordinate space. Gradient/pattern opacity is independent per use. Gradient spreading and monotonically clamped stop offsets are honored. RGB alpha/channel clamping, quoted local paint/filter references and explicit inheritance of non-inherited CSS properties are handled correctly. currentColor, gradient-stop styling, transform origin, variables and animation declarations participate in improved CSS handling. Verification and scope All nine library targets build without warnings/errors. WPF regressions, live clocks and 14 external animation examples pass. Selected checks use resvg-test-suite revision d8e0643: 200 reference-image comparisons and four render-only cases with nonportable/undefined expectations. Tolerances account for WPF antialiasing, tiled edges and fractional morphology radii. Blur uses separable box convolutions; morphology uses sliding extrema. Raster filters are capped at 2048 pixels on their longest dimension and sample sources at load time. Single matrix/saturation filters can retain vector paints to preserve native clocks. A plain-WPF rendering preflight reports an unavailable Windows graphics session before SVG pixel checks run. Implementation: CSS, geometry, patterns, motion and procedural filters, filter graphs, paths and colors. 2026-10-28 Added Native animation: WPF clocks for SMIL transforms, timed visibility/display, opacity, circle/ellipse radii/centers and root viewBox cameras. Numeric starts, repeats, freeze, key times, splines and explicit click starts are supported. CSS keyframes: transform/opacity and stepped sprite-sheet playback, including the extracted CodePen horse example. Host controls: UseAnimations, deterministic SeekAnimations snapshots and TriggerAnimationEvent. Changing the source after initialization respects the animation setting. Fixed Symbol/use viewBoxes, dimensions, alignment and aspect ratios now render correctly, fixing facial-part placement in MattHead and PeteyHead. Static color-matrix/saturation paint mappings support Flash2Svg exports while preserving native drawing animation. Implementation: native animation. 5.2.16 — 2026-10-28 Added Luminance/alpha masks, mask/content units, region clipping, percentages, transforms, styled/forward references, nesting and safe empty/cyclic references. White/alpha masks keep vector drawing where possible; colored luminance masks use composited raster conversion. Fixed The SVG from #118 renders with its intended mask. Its fixture checks 93,767 flat interior pixels against Chromium. Implementation: SVG masks. 5.2.15 — 2026-10-28 Added IsGrayscale and DrawingColorConverter.ToGrayscale cover solid/gradient brushes, strokes, groups and bitmaps. Frozen drawings remain shareable. Addresses #99. Fixed RGB/percentage RGB gradient stops are parsed correctly. Addresses #116. SVG button content has an intrinsic desired size without explicit dimensions. Addresses #106. Implementation: RGB gradients, button sizing, grayscale. 5.2.14 — 2026-10-28 Incorporated the upstream duplicate-font-name correction from #121, originally authored in March 2026. Earlier history For earlier changes, see the release tags and commit history. Historical versions are not reconstructed as release notes here. GettingStarted.html.title: Get started | SVGImage
GettingStarted.html.summary: Get started SVGImage is a Windows WPF control and renderer. The source targets .NET Framework 4.0–4.8, .NET Core 3.1 and .NET 6–8 for Windows. Install a published package dotnet add package DotNetProjects.SVGImage See NuGet for versions. The support reference describes the current source; unreleased changes may not yet be packaged. Put an SVG in your window Add the SVG to your application, set its build action to Content and copy it to the output directory. Add the namespace and control: <Window x:Class="MyApp.MainWindow" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation" xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml" xmlns:svg="https://github.com/dotnetprojects/SVGImage"> <svg:SVGImage UriSource="Assets/illustration.svg" Width="320" Height="240" UseAnimations="True" SizeType="ViewBoxToSizeNoStretch" /> </Window> UseAnimations defaults to true. Set it to false for static rendering. Color overrides include OverrideColor, OverrideFillColor and OverrideStrokeColor. Set IsGrayscale="True" for grayscale display. Work with a Drawing For direct drawing access, opt in to animation before loading: var renderer = new SVGImage.SVG.SVGRender { UseAnimations = true }; System.Windows.Media.DrawingGroup drawing = renderer.LoadDrawing("Assets/illustration.svg"); // Stop the existing drawing at an exact time for a snapshot. renderer.SeekAnimations(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1.5)); Reload/recreate the drawing to restart playback after seeking. See animation controls and the API reference. Build the current source Use Source/SVGImage.sln with Visual Studio 2022, or build on Windows: dotnet build Source/SVGImage/DotNetProjects.SVGImage.csproj -p:GeneratePackageOnBuild=false To use unreleased changes, reference the library project or a matching locally built DLL instead of an older package. Explore the samples, support reference and changelog.

Grayscale.html.title: Grayscale rendering | SVGImage
Grayscale.html.summary: Grayscale rendering Set IsGrayscale to display an SVG in grayscale without replacing every color with the same value: <svg:SVGImage UriSource="/Images/icon.svg" IsGrayscale="True" /> The conversion preserves alpha, gradient stops, strokes, and vector geometry. Embedded bitmap images are converted to grayscale with their alpha preserved. Color overrides are applied before conversion. Set IsGrayscale back to False to display the original colors. To obtain and modify a rendered drawing yourself, use SVGRender: var renderer = new SVGImage.SVG.SVGRender(); Drawing original = renderer.LoadDrawing("icon.svg"); Drawing gray = SVGImage.SVG.Utils.DrawingColorConverter.ToGrayscale(original); svgControl.SetImage(gray); // Or use new DrawingImage(gray) as a WPF ImageSource. ToGrayscale returns a copy, so the original drawing can be shared with other controls. It uses the weighted RGB luminance 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B. Drawings with active animations are converted at their current values.

Masks.html.title: SVG masks | SVGImage
Masks.html.summary: SVG masks SVGImage supports local mask references on shapes, groups, use elements and the root SVG: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100" height="100"> <defs> <mask id="cutout"> <rect width="100" height="100" fill="white" /> <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="20" fill="black" /> </mask> </defs> <rect width="100" height="100" fill="red" mask="url(#cutout)" /> </svg> White reveals the artwork, black hides it, and gray or translucent content partially reveals it. Mask content is composited before luminance is multiplied by alpha, so a black shape painted over white cuts a hole. color-interpolation="linearRGB" selects linear RGB luminance; the default is sRGB. mask-type="alpha" uses alpha alone. Both maskUnits and maskContentUnits support userSpaceOnUse and objectBoundingBox. Defaults follow SVG: the region uses the object's geometry bounding box, excluding stroke, with x="-10%", y="-10%", width="120%" and height="120%"; content uses the target's user coordinates. Bounding-box content accepts normalized numbers and percentages. Region clipping, child transforms, inherited fills, forward references and nested masks are supported. Definitions do not paint directly. Empty masks, zero/negative regions and cyclic mask references produce no visible content. White-only luminance masks and alpha masks remain vector drawings. Colored luminance masks are composited into an offscreen bitmap, with the longest side between 1024 and 2048 pixels, then used as a WPF opacity mask. At very large zoom levels these colored masks can show raster sampling. Mask contents are evaluated when the drawing is created; animated masks and external-document mask references are not implemented. Masking uses the graphics features already supported by SVGImage, so unsupported SVG filters and other unsupported child elements retain their existing limitations. OverrideColor, OverrideFillColor, OverrideStrokeColor and OverrideStrokeWidth affect the visible artwork without changing mask colors or geometry. Reference: SVG 1.1 masking.

Rendering.html.title: SVG geometry and raster filters | SVGImage
Rendering.html.summary: SVG geometry and raster filters Clipping accepts paths, basic shapes, text and local use references. Child silhouettes are united, clip-rule is inherited, transforms are applied, and clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox" maps normalized content to the target's geometric bounds. Empty clips hide their targets. Definitions and circular references do not paint. Nested svg elements establish independent percentage-length contexts, viewport position/dimensions, viewBoxes, meet/slice/none aspect ratios and overflow clipping. Symbol viewBoxes also establish the percentage context for their content. Local use references preserve their target's parent after rendering and circular references are ignored. textPath lays out glyph outlines along a referenced path, rotates them to the path tangent, and supports startOffset (including percentages), text anchoring and nested styled spans. Glyphs whose midpoints are outside the path are omitted. This does not implement text stretching/automatic spacing, vertical text-on-path or pathLength calibration. Patterns support independent patternUnits and patternContentUnits, tile origin/dimensions, viewBox/aspect ratio, transforms, opacity and local href templates (including forward references). Brushes are constructed per target bounds, so sharing a pattern between differently sized objects is safe. Circular pattern painting returns transparent content. Pattern overflow is clipped to the tile. feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap use a bounded CPU raster pipeline. Turbulence provides four seeded channels, turbulence/fractalNoise, one or two base frequencies, up to nine octaves and tile stitching, using the SVG 1.1 noise generator. Displacement uses unpremultiplied R/G/B/A selectors, signed scale and bilinear sampling with transparent pixels outside the input. Standalone filters and chains support SourceGraphic/SourceAlpha, named results, primitive subregions, filter/primitive coordinate units, sRGB/linearRGB conversion, flood, offset, merge, composite, color matrices (including saturation, hue rotation and luminance-to-alpha), component transfer, blend, Gaussian blur, morphology and tile. Component transfer implements identity, linear, gamma, table and discrete functions on unpremultiplied channels. Blend implements separable and nonseparable CSS blend modes. Gaussian blur uses three separable box convolutions, keeping work linear in the image size even for large radii. Morphology uses sliding extrema for erosion/dilation. Tile repeats the input subregion, including its transparent pixels. Unsupported primitive types are currently passed through; this is not a complete SVG filter graph implementation. Single matrix/saturation filters retain a vector paint mapping when native animations are enabled to preserve child clocks. Element opacity is applied after the filter; fill/stroke opacity is part of SourceGraphic. Radial gradients retain their focal point in the same coordinate space as the center, and gradient/pattern brushes preserve per-use opacity. CSS colors accept RGB/RGBA, HSL/HSLA, percentage channels and short/long RGBA hex notation. Gradient stops clamp offsets monotonically, and gradients honor pad/repeat/reflect spreading. SVG path data is parsed segment by segment, including single-token adjacent arc flags and reflected curve controls. Invalid data stops the current path at its last complete segment instead of aborting the SVG. Polygon/polyline lists likewise retain valid pairs before invalid data and ignore an unmatched final coordinate. Empty paths and point lists are safe. Raster filters sample the source at load time; animation of the filtered source or filter parameters does not update their bitmap. Rasterization uses up to four pixels per user unit and a maximum dimension of 2048 pixels. This bounds memory use but limits magnification quality. The geometry and animation features remain vector-based outside these raster filter chains. Run the regression runner with RESVG_TEST_SUITE pointing to a local checkout of linebender/resvg-test-suite to additionally compare path, polygon/polyline and supported filter cases against its reference PNGs. The huge-blur, transformed-tile and two out-of-range saturation fixtures are checked for successful rendering only: the huge-blur reference has implementation-specific artifacts and the other fixtures are explicitly marked undefined behavior upstream. Image comparisons allow small rasterization differences, with a wider tolerance for repeated tile edges and fractional morphology radii. Reference SVGs/PNGs and downloaded animation examples are kept outside this repository.

api/SVGImage.SVG.SVGImage.eSizeType.html.summary: Enum SVGImage.eSizeType Namespace SVGImage.SVG Assembly DotNetProjects.SVGImage.dll This controls how the image is stretched to fill the control, public enum SVGImage.eSizeType Fields ContentToSizeNoStretch = 1 The image is scaled to fit the control without any stretching. Either X or Y direction will be scaled to fill the entire width or height. ContentToSizeStretch = 2 The image will be stretched to fill the entire width and height. None = 0 The image is not scaled. The image location is translated so the top left corner of the image bounding box is moved to the top left corner of the image control. SizeToContent = 3 The control will be resized to fit the un-scaled image. If the image is larger than the maximum size for the control, the control is set to maximum size and the image is scaled. ViewBoxToSizeNoStretch = 4 Not the content of the image but its viewbox is scaled to fit the control without any stretching. Either X or Y direction will be scaled to fill the entire width or height.

Percent = 1 Percent is relative to least distant viewbox dimensions. If the length is inherently horizontal, like "dx", then the percentage is relative to the least distant viewbox width. api/SVGImage.SVG.Shapes.WritingMode.html.summary: Enum WritingMode Namespace SVGImage.SVG.Shapes Assembly DotNetProjects.SVGImage.dll The ‘writing-mode’ property specifies whether the initial inline-progression-direction for a ‘text’ element shall be left-to-right, right-to-left, or top-to-bottom. The ‘writing-mode’ property applies only to ‘text’ elements; the property is ignored for ‘tspan’, ‘tref’, ‘altGlyph’ and ‘textPath’ sub-elements. (Note that the inline-progression-direction can change within a ‘text’ element due to the Unicode bidirectional algorithm and properties ‘direction’ and ‘unicode-bidi’. For more on bidirectional text, see Relationship with bidirectionality.) public enum WritingMode Fields HorizontalTopToBottom = 1 This value defines a top-to-bottom block flow direction. Both the writing mode and the typographic mode are horizontal. Set for atrributes with values 'horizontal-tb', 'lr', 'lr-tb', 'rl', and 'rl-tb'. articles/intro.html.title: | SVGImage
articles/intro.html.summary: Introduction SVG (Scalable Vector Graphic) is an XML based graphic format. This little project started out as a simple SVG to XAML converter. I looked at some simple SVG files and noticed the similarity to XAML defined graphic, and decided to write a converter. However, I soon realized that SVG is a very complex format, and at the same time, I found no good reason for converting to XAML just to show the image on the screen, so instead, I started working on the SVG, SVGRender and the SVGImage classes. The SVG class is the class that reads and parses the XML file. SVGRender is the class that creates the WPF Drawing object based on the information from the SVG class. SVGImage is the image control. The image control can either load the image from a filename SetImage(filename) or by setting the Drawing object through SetImage(Drawing), which allows multiple controls to share the same drawing instance. The control only has a couple of properties, SizeType and ImageSource. SizeType - controls how the image is stretched to fill the control None: The image is not scaled. The image location is translated so the top left corner of the image bounding box is moved to the top left corner of the image control. ContentToSizeNoStretch: The image is scaled to fit the control without any stretching. Either X or Y direction will be scaled to fill the entire width or height. ContentToSizeStretch: The image will be stretched to fill the entire width and height. SizeToContent: The control will be resized to fit the un-scaled image. If the image is larger than the max size for the control, the control is set to max size and the image is scaled. ViewBoxToSizeNoStretch: Not the content of the image but its viewbox is scaled to fit the control without any stretching.Either X or Y direction will be scaled to fill the entire width or height. For None and ContentToSizeNoStretch, the Horizontal/VerticalContentAlignment properties can be used to position the image within the control. ImageSource - This property is the same as SetImage(drawing), and is exposed to allow for the source to be set through binding. The colors of an SVGImage can be overridden at run-time through some additional properties of the SVGImage: OverrideFillColor - This property overrides all fill colors of an SVG image OverrideStrokeColor - Overrides all stroke colors of an SVG image OverrideColor - Overrides all colors of an SVG image. OverrideFillColor and OverrideStrokeColor take precedence over the OverrideColor property.
